name: scan-flash-sweep
concept: A brief bright flash sweeps through the element as if a scan line passed over it, continuous. Use it for a scanner or processing indicator that has no moving part.

name: scan-pulse-line
concept: Brightness rises and falls twice each cycle, like a scan beam sweeping back and forth. Fits a barcode reader or a repeated-pass scanning motif.

name: scan-glow-pass
concept: A gentle glow brightens the element midway through the cycle, then fades. Use it for an ambient, low-key scanning cue instead of a sharp flash.

name: scan-dim-sweep
concept: A shadow dims the element midway through the cycle, the inverse of a bright scan. Use it on light backgrounds where a bright flash would not read well.

name: scan-soft-pass
concept: Brightness and opacity rise and fall smoothly across five stops, a gradual scan pass. Use it where a subtle, unhurried scanning cue fits the tone.

name: scan-sharp-pass
concept: A short, high-contrast flash snaps through the element at the midpoint of each cycle. Use it for a crisp, mechanical scan such as an ID or code reader.

name: scan-reverse-sweep
concept: Brightness jumps up fast then decays slowly across the rest of the cycle, a reversed scan rhythm. Use it where an even scan feels too uniform.

name: scan-corner-sweep
concept: A brightness pulse pairs with a slight skew, suggesting a scan passing across at an angle. Use it for a document or page scan with a diagonal feel.

name: shimmer-vertical
concept: A soft gradient highlight sweeps top to bottom, continuous. Reads as a placeholder standing in for content, like shimmer but along the vertical axis. Requires a vertically oriented gradient background-image and background-size: 100% 200%.

name: shimmer-vertical-reverse
concept: The gradient highlight sweeps from bottom to top, the reverse of a standard vertical shimmer. Use it when content loads or reveals upward on the page. Needs the same vertical gradient background setup as shimmer-vertical.

name: shimmer-vertical-soft
concept: The vertical gradient sweep holds briefly at each end before moving, a gentler pace than the standard vertical shimmer. Use it for calmer, low-emphasis skeleton screens. Requires the same vertical gradient background setup.

name: shimmer-vertical-fade
concept: The vertical gradient sweep pairs with an opacity dip and rise, fading as it passes. Use it where a plain vertical shimmer feels too flat. Requires the same vertical gradient background setup as shimmer-vertical.

name: shimmer-vertical-bounce
concept: The vertical gradient overshoots past its endpoint before settling, a light bounce at the end of the sweep. Use it for a more playful skeleton loading state. Requires the same vertical gradient background setup as shimmer-vertical.

name: shimmer-vertical-pause
concept: The gradient sweeps down then holds at the bottom before snapping back, a pause between passes. Use it where a beat of stillness reads better than constant motion. Requires the same vertical gradient background setup as shimmer-vertical.

name: shimmer-vertical-tight
concept: A narrower gradient band sweeps top to bottom, a tighter highlight than the standard vertical shimmer. Use it on short elements where a wide band would look wrong. Requires a vertical gradient background-image and background-size: 100% 140%.

name: radar-scan
concept: A ring grows outward and fades, then restarts before the fade fully finishes, an ongoing radar-style scan. Use it for a searching or scanning state, not a single alert ping.

name: radar-scan-tight
concept: The ring grows only a little before fading, a tighter and more subtle radar sweep. Use it inside small elements where a wide radar-scan would overflow.

name: radar-scan-wide
concept: The ring expands much further before fading, a wide, sweeping radar scan. Use it on larger elements where a bigger reach reads better.

name: radar-scan-fast
concept: The ring expands and fades quickly with fewer stops, a brisk radar scan. Use it where a standard radar scan feels too slow for the context.

name: radar-scan-slow
concept: The ring expands gradually across five stops, a slow and methodical radar scan. Use it for a deliberate, careful searching state.

name: radar-pulse-scan
concept: A small bump interrupts the ring's growth partway through, like two overlapping pulses in one sweep. Use it for a busier, more active scanning feel.

name: radar-scan-soft
concept: The ring's growth pairs with a gentle brightness lift, a softer radar scan than a plain scale-and-fade. Use it for an ambient, low-contrast scanning cue.

name: fill-loop
concept: A bar grows from empty to full, then resets and grows again, continuous. Use it for a working state when there is no real percentage to report.

name: fill-loop-fast
concept: The bar fills quickly, holds briefly at full, then snaps back to empty. Use it for a brisk, repeated working cue.

name: fill-loop-slow
concept: The bar fills in three gradual stages before resetting, a slower and more deliberate fill loop. Use it for a longer working process.

name: fill-hold-reset
concept: The bar reaches full and holds there for most of the cycle before resetting. Use it where a lingering full state reads as work being reviewed or finalized.

name: fill-fade-reset
concept: The bar fills to full, then fades out instead of snapping back, before reappearing empty. Use it for a softer reset than a visible snap.

name: fill-bounce-loop
concept: The bar overshoots past full, settles back, then resets, a light bounce at the end of the fill. Use it for a livelier working indicator.

name: fill-step-loop
concept: The bar grows in four distinct steps rather than smoothly, a chunky, quantized fill. Use it to suggest discrete stages of work instead of a continuous flow.

name: fill-elastic-loop
concept: The bar oscillates around full before settling, like an elastic band coming to rest, then resets. Use it for a springy, energetic working cue.

name: shimmer-double-sweep
concept: The gradient highlight sweeps across twice per cycle with a short gap between passes. Use it where a single shimmer pass feels too sparse.

name: shimmer-double-tight
concept: Two shimmer passes follow each other with only a brief gap, a tighter double sweep. Use it for a busier, more energetic loading cue.

name: shimmer-double-wide
concept: Two shimmer passes are separated by a longer pause, a more spaced double sweep. Use it for a calmer loading cue that still reads as ongoing.

name: shimmer-double-fast
concept: Two shimmer passes fire quickly one after another early in the cycle, then the highlight holds still until the loop restarts. Use it for a brief, energetic burst of activity.

name: shimmer-double-fade
concept: The gradient sweeps across, dims briefly, then sweeps again, a double pass with a fade between them. Use it to add a beat of rest between two shimmer sweeps.

name: shimmer-double-stagger
concept: The second shimmer pass begins before the first fully completes, an overlapping, staggered sweep. Use it for a denser, layered loading effect.

name: reading-wave-sweep
concept: Opacity and a slight sideways shift rise and fall once per cycle, suggesting content being read left to right. Use it for text or list content that is being processed in order.

name: reading-wave-slow
concept: The opacity wave rises and falls gradually across five stops, a slower, more methodical reading pace. Use it for careful, line-by-line processing cues.

name: reading-wave-step
concept: Opacity and position jump between two fixed points rather than flowing smoothly, like eyes jumping between words. Use it for a more mechanical reading cue.

name: reading-wave-pause
concept: Opacity rises to full and holds there before falling, a pause as if dwelling on a line. Use it for a deliberate, comprehension-style reading cue.

name: saccade-scan
concept: Opacity and position jump quickly between two points with short pauses, mimicking the rapid eye movements used when scanning text. Use it for a fast, natural reading or review cue.

name: processing-wave
concept: Opacity and brightness rise and fall once per cycle at a measured pace, suggesting quiet background processing. Use it for tasks that are working steadily but not urgently.

name: reading-wave-soft
concept: Opacity and position shift only slightly across the cycle, a low-amplitude version of the reading wave. Use it where a strong wave would distract from the content.

name: flicker-scan
concept: Opacity flickers rapidly through the first half of the cycle, then settles, a quick scanning burst. Use it for a fast, energetic scan cue at the start of a loop.

name: flicker-scan-fast
concept: Opacity flickers in a tight burst within the first fifth of the cycle, faster than the standard flicker scan. Use it for a snappier, more urgent scan cue.

name: flicker-scan-strobe
concept: Opacity strobes evenly across the whole cycle at regular intervals, unlike a front-loaded flicker scan. Use it for a constant, alert-style scanning cue.

name: flicker-scan-double
concept: Two short flicker bursts fire with a calm gap between them, a double-burst scanning rhythm. Use it where a single flicker burst feels too brief.

name: flicker-scan-quick
concept: The element stays steady through most of the cycle, then flickers briefly right before the loop restarts. Use it as a quick heads-up cue just before a refresh.

name: flicker-scan-energetic
concept: Opacity flickers pair with brightness boosts at irregular points through the cycle, a more energetic scan than a plain opacity flicker. Use it for a lively, attention-grabbing loading cue.

name: flicker-scan-rapid
concept: Opacity flickers evenly and rapidly across the entire cycle at the highest frequency in this set. Use it for an intense, high-energy scanning cue.
